Inua Jamii means “lift the community.”

Lifting communities, one family at a time.

Inua Jamii Foundation supports people in need with food, health care, education and the tools to earn a living. We work with communities, not for them, so that help lasts.

About us

Who we are, why we exist and how we work.

Our story

Inua Jamii Foundation began when neighbours decided not to wait for help from outside. They pooled what they had to feed hungry families and keep children in school. Today we are an organisation that supports people in need across our community.

We still work the same way: listen first, act together and measure what changes.

Mission

To help people in need meet their basic needs and build the skills and confidence to support themselves.

Vision

A community where every person can live in dignity and no family is left behind.

What we value

Dignity

We treat everyone as a partner with strengths to build on.

Accountability

We report openly on how funds are used and what they achieve.

Collaboration

We work with local leaders, schools, clinics and other organisations.

Compassion

We respond to need with care and without judgement.

Our journey

  • Year oneNeighbours organise the first food drive.
  • Year threeWe register as a foundation and open our first school support programme.
  • Year fiveHealth outreach and livelihood training begin.
  • TodayThousands of people reached every year across five focus areas.

Our work

Five programmes that work together to meet urgent needs and build long-term stability.

Food and nutrition

No child learns or grows well on an empty stomach. We provide emergency food parcels and support school meals for families facing hunger.

  • Monthly food parcels for families in crisis
  • School feeding for children
  • Nutrition education for parents

Health and wellbeing

We bring basic care closer to people who cannot afford to travel or pay for it.

  • Community health days and screenings
  • Health education on hygiene, maternal and child health
  • Referrals and support with medical costs

Education

Education is the surest way out of poverty. We remove the costs that keep children out of class.

  • School fees and uniforms
  • Books and learning materials
  • Mentoring and catch-up classes

Livelihoods

We help adults earn a steady income so families can support themselves.

  • Skills training in trades and business
  • Small start-up grants and savings groups
  • Mentoring for new entrepreneurs

Clean water and shelter

Safe water and a secure home protect health and dignity.

  • Water points and water-storage support
  • Sanitation facilities
  • Repairs for unsafe homes

How we measure

We track who we reach, what changes in their lives and whether the change lasts. Community members review our results with us each year, and we publish what we learn, including what did not work.

Inua Jamii School

Quality learning in a safe, caring place, so every child can reach their potential.

A school built by and for the community

Inua Jamii School is the Foundation’s own school. It gives children from families in need a safe place to learn, grow and discover what they can do.

Fees are kept low, and sponsorship covers children whose families cannot pay, so no child is turned away because of money.

Ask about admission

The school at a glance

450learners
25learners per class, on average
18teachers and staff

Why families choose us

Learning works best when children feel safe, fed and supported.

Caring teachers

Trained teachers who know every child by name and expect the best from them.

A safe, welcoming campus

A secure place where children can play and learn without worry.

Meals and health

A daily meal and regular health checks keep children ready to learn.

Sponsorship

Donors cover fees, uniforms and books for children who need help.

Levels we teach

Children grow through clear stages, each with its own care and challenge.

Early years

Play-based learning that builds language, number skills and confidence.

Primary

Strong foundations in reading, maths, science and the arts.

Junior school

Skills, projects and guidance that prepare learners for the next step.

How to join

  • Make an enquiryContact us or visit the school office.
  • Visit the schoolMeet the teachers and see the classrooms.
  • ApplyFill in the admission form and share the required documents.
  • Start learningJoin us for a welcome day, then the first day of term.

Admissions

Open to children from the surrounding community. Sponsorship is available for families who cannot pay fees.
